examples.name: trombone slide, slow and surrendering
examples.physical_system: trombone — heavy slide, long air column, brass damps overshoot
examples.teaching_note: Smooth exponential approach — no overshoot, no ripple. Listen for the lack of arrival 'thump'.

examples.name: theremin glide, hand drifting through space
examples.physical_system: theremin — capacitive coupling, no mechanical inertia, glide rate set by hand motion
examples.teaching_note: Heavy overdamping. The pitch sneaks up on the target. Theremins almost always sound this way.

examples.name: cello slow portamento between long notes
examples.physical_system: cello — bowed string, finger slides slowly with steady bow
examples.teaching_note: String harmonics ride the smooth glide. No overshoot — the bow stabilizes the trajectory.

examples.name: lap steel sustained slide
examples.physical_system: pedal/lap steel — heavy bar, slow controlled finger motion
examples.teaching_note: Even heavier damping than the cello — clearly languid, surrender-like.

examples.name: purposeful synth glide
examples.physical_system: synthesizer — engineered glide circuit tuned for fastest no-overshoot arrival
examples.teaching_note: Arrives decisively and stops. No ringing, no lag. Classic Moog-style portamento.

examples.name: trained singer landing on the note
examples.physical_system: trained vocalist — disciplined laryngeal control, arrives without overshoot
examples.teaching_note: A controlled vocal arrival — no perceptible overshoot. Compare to example #10 (untrained singer).

examples.name: kalimba tine settling after pluck
examples.physical_system: kalimba — tine has high stiffness and clamped boundary, settles fast
examples.teaching_note: The settling time is very short — a quick decisive arrival, almost like a plucked attack.

examples.name: acoustic guitar string bend, controlled release
examples.physical_system: guitar — bend released with discipline, string tension settles fast
examples.teaching_note: Downward critically-damped — same regime, different direction. Listen for the lack of ring-back.

examples.name: bell strike, retuned by a transient blow
examples.physical_system: bell — light strike that detunes; resonance rings around target
examples.teaching_note: Underdamped + inharmonic. The pitch rings BELOW target and bounces back — hear the wobble.

examples.name: untrained singer overshooting from below
examples.physical_system: untrained vocalist — laryngeal muscle ramp overshoots; settles slightly flat then sharp
examples.teaching_note: Audible overshoot above the target, then settle. This is the *characteristic* aliveness of an untrained voice.

examples.name: electric guitar fast bend with finger vibrato
examples.physical_system: guitar — fast bend, string tension overshoots, finger relaxes back
examples.teaching_note: Listen for the sharp arrival then return — this is the 'cry' character of an expressive bend.

examples.name: prepared piano string — complex inharmonic settling
examples.physical_system: prepared piano — object on string changes mode geometry, each mode rings at its own rate
examples.teaching_note: Multi-modal: each harmonic settles at its own zeta/wn. The TIMBRE changes during the glide.
